messages:
Sam Rivera: FYI acme legal just pushed a SIG/CAIQ request + DPA redline. They want the CAIQ answers by EOD and a crisp note on DSAR/deletion timelines. I'm on the POC. Can someone own the CAIQ and DPA language?
Priya Nair: tagging @Dante and @Maya. I can take CAIQ controls around auth, key mgmt, and network isolation. Need to know which deployment we promised for the POC (hosted vs dedicated vs private).
Dante Liu: POC is on Dedicated (reserved capacity) in us-west-2 per infra ticket. We'll have customer traffic routed to dedicated pool, not hosted sandbox. Logs are currently enabled for debugging but can be scoped/disabled.
Sam Rivera: good — they specifically asked that PII used during the POC be deleted on request and that DSARs are feasible. Also asking if we support SCCs and whether the DPA language maps to SCCs.
Maya Patel: For the DPA: suggest we propose this short clause to start with —

```
Data subject requests: Redwood Inference will assist Customer with DSARs and will, upon Customer's instruction, delete inference request data stored by Redwood within 30 days of receipt of a deletion request unless otherwise required by law. Customer retains control to request permanent purge of data from ephemeral caches and retained logs.
```

Maya Patel: On SCCs: we have standard SCCs in our enterprise pack; legal can confirm. For the CAIQ, I can handle privacy-related questions (4.x retention, 5.x access).
Priya Nair: I'll take encryption/KMS, segmentation, and incident response (A.03, A.05 in CAIQ). Quick question — Dante, do we persist KV cache to disk in Dedicated POC or only in-memory across GPUs?
Dante Liu: KV cache is in-memory by default for the runtime; we checkpoint model artifacts but not per-request KV to durable storage. For debugging we do a temporary capture to a secure S3 bucket (encrypted, access-logged). That capture can be disabled.
Priya Nair: perfect — I'll note "no persistent per-request KV storage" in CAIQ and add the temporary-capture caveat.
Sam Rivera: Customer also asked for a single-paragraph operational summary they can hand to their InfoSec: "what we store, retention, deletion options, who to contact" — can we get that by 6pm PST?
Maya Patel: Draft for review: "Redwood Inference processes inference requests for Customer. Per-request inputs and outputs are processed in-memory and not persisted to durable storage by default. Temporary debugging captures are encrypted at rest and access-controlled; these can be disabled upon Customer request. DSAR and deletion requests can be initiated via Customer Support or API and will be actioned within 30 days. For Dedicated and Private deployments, Customer can configure stricter retention or request permanent purge."
Sam Rivera: that reads well. I'll paste it into the DPA redline and send to acme legal after we finalize CAIQ answers.
Priya Nair: I'll upload a completed CAIQ worksheet to the shared folder (drive link) and flag any items that need infra/legal signoff.
Dante Liu: I'll schedule the POC run with logging disabled and provide the exact S3 paths we used for captures so Legal can confirm deletion steps.
LegalBot: Document created: "sales/acme/CAIQ-completed-1729965432" — please review and attach to the redline PR.
Sam Rivera: next steps: Priya completes CAIQ by 3pm, Maya finalizes DPA paragraph + one-paragraph summary by 4:30, Dante provides capture paths + switches by 5pm, I send to customer by 6pm. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Maya Patel: added a short DSAR runbook snippet to the draft — includes contact email, expected timelines, and confirmation step after purge. Will ping legal if we need stronger wording.
Priya Nair: noted a couple CAIQ items where we reference Dedicated vs Hosted behaviors — added comments for product to confirm.
Dante Liu: I'll do a quick run in staging to validate capture disable flag and report back with a one-liner to paste in the CAIQ.
Sam Rivera: Great — if anything slips, @me. Otherwise I'll queue the email once everything's attached.
Maya Patel: I'm available for redline call if acme pushes back on the 30-day DSAR timeline.
Sam Rivera: thanks team, closing thread after uploads.
